method: Primary sources only: Hansard, the Commons Votes record, official responses, and members' own words in their own channels. Press coverage is linked as context and labelled as press. Quotes are verbatim. No scores, no verdicts.

records.title: Voted No on proscribing Palestine Action
Commons debate: Prevention and Suppression of Terrorism
records.quote: Surely we should be looking at the issue that Palestine Action is concerned about, as well as the supply of weapons from this country to Israel, which has made all that possible.

records.title: Asked for separate votes on the three groups in the order
records.quote: I and many others outside, I am sure, think it would be fair if we took individual votes on the three.

records.title: Voted No on proscribing Palestine Action
Speech against the order. The official report ends mid-sentence
records.quote: So I say this loudly and proudly on Wednesday 2 July 2025—
records.note: This is the last line of her speech as printed in Hansard. She says she finished the sentence with “We are all Palestine Action” before the Chair intervened.

records.title: Says Parliament and Hansard removed the words from her speech
records.quote: Parliament and Hansard have removed “We are all Palestine Action” from my speech on Wednesday 2 July 2025 — despite me saying it.

records.title: Point of order putting the words on the record; the Chair replies
records.quote: In my speech on Wednesday 2 July 2025 during the debate on the prevention and suppression of terrorism, I said the words, “We are all Palestine Action.”

reply.quote: Hansard has its own editorial policy. If she wishes to have her words corrected, she needs to take that up directly with Hansard. That is not a responsibility of the Chair.

records.title: House of Commons explains the omission in a freedom-of-information reply
records.quote: The remark was made after the Deputy Speaker had said ‘Order’, because of that limit. It is standard practice for the Hansard record to stop when the Chair intervenes to bring a speech to an end when the time limit has been reached.

sources.label: House of Commons FOI reply, via WhatDoTheyKnow
